FINAL SUBMISSION

## What I changed
A targeted weight edit on all 24 transformer blocks, saved in `/work/edited` (backup in `/work/best_C`):

For every layer L in 0–23: `down_proj.weight ← down_proj.weight − 0.04 · outer(u_w, b̂_L)`
- `u_w = normalize(E[13428] + E[13784]) ⊙ (1 + γ)` — the unit readout direction of " Wait"/"Wait" (token ids 13428/13784, the verification-spiral openers) through the tied embedding and the (1+γ) RMSNorm;
- `b_L = mean MLP input activation at Wait-loop positions − mean at normal positions`, measured with a teacher-forced pass on a real Wait-loop failure (math/intermediate_algebra/512-style re-derivation spiral); `b̂_L` is its unit normalization.

Nothing else changed: final norm, embeddings/output layer, attention, gate/up projections and the prior "close thinking" edit are all intact. Edit magnitude is 0.04 per singular direction (~0.04 of one unit column), nowhere near tensor norms.

## The failure I diagnosed (from this run's measurements)
Starting weights: ~49% select accuracy; ~28% of generations hit the 8192-token limit (all wrong); 34% no-boxed. Cut-off answers split into (a) infinite "Wait, let me check…" re-derivation spirals that never close thinking, and (b) post-`</think>` infinite `</think>` cascades. Attribution passes showed the `</think>` pressure is a smooth, distributed, depth-growing signal, not a single component; u-amplification is a cliff edge (it caused mid-word `</think>` emissions — I tested that and got −32.8pp, so I reverted it). The Wait-loop states, by contrast, are linearly separable with the model sitting only 1–2 logits from emitting "Wait" at each spiral step — a separable, low-margin state, ideal for a gentle rank-one push away from it.

## Evidence it helps (paired vs original, same problems, fixed seeds)
| split (64 problems × n=2) | Δ acc | cut rate | no-boxed |
|---|---|---|---|
| select[0:64] | +3.12pp (SE 3.12) | 37.5→29.7% | 43→34% |
| confirm_1[0:64] | +7.03pp (SE 2.92) | 42.2→32.0% | 46.9→37.5% |
| confirm_1[64:128] | +11.2pp (SE 5.19) | 40.3→27.4% | 44.4→29.0% |
| confirm_2[0:64] | −2.34pp (SE 4.78) | 32.0→18.8% | 35.2→24.2% |
| confirm_2[64:128] | +5.47pp (SE 2.97) | 32.0→25.0% | 39.8→29.7% |

Pooled over 636 paired answers: **≈ +4.9pp (SE ≈ 1.75), 73 wrong→right vs 43 right→wrong**. Cut-off and no-boxed shares drop in all five splits; generations retain complete thinking (mean tokens −8–13% only; short-answer fraction unchanged). The one slightly negative subset was the highest-accuracy (easiest) split — the edit helps hardest on low-accuracy, hard competition problems, the MATH-500 regime.

## Expected effect and caveats
Expect ~+3 to +6 points over the starting weights on unseen MATH-500-like problems, driven by converting truncated/spiraling non-answers into finished, boxed answers. The effect size is chaos-noisy per problem (dose-response non-monotonic), and the no-boxed "\boxed-less prose answer" bucket (~4%) remains the biggest unexploited opportunity — but the evidence above is from untouched confirmation splits, measured with the evaluation's protocol, with the final candidate chosen before any confirmation run.
